Rashi on Eruvin 63a:10:1.hebrew: דאתחילו בכבודו - מאחר שנאמר לו: "דניחוש לסבא", והתחילו לדבר בכבודו — לא היה לו לזלזל בדבר:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:10:1.english: Since they had begun with his honor - Since it was said to him: “Let us show concern for the elder,” and they had begun to speak of his honor, he should not have treated the matter lightly.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:11:1.hebrew: ואב"א שאני רב אחא בר יעקב דמפליג - הרבה מאד היה זקן וחכם:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:11:1.english: And if you wish, say: Rav Aḥa bar Ya’akov is different, as he was illustrious - He was exceedingly elderly and wise.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:12:1.hebrew: ולאפרושי מאיסורא - ראה תלמיד אדם רוצה לעבור עבירה, ורבו שם ושותק — מותר לתלמיד לקפוץ ולגעור:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:12:1.english: And to separate [someone] from a prohibition - [If] a disciple saw a person wanting to commit a transgression, and his teacher was there and silent — it is permitted for the disciple to jump in and rebuke [him].

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:12:2.hebrew: בצינתא - בדקל, ואין משתמשין באילן משום שבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:12:2.english: To a palm tree - To a palm tree; and one may not make use of a tree [on Shabbat] due to a rabbinic decree [shevut].

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:13:1.hebrew: אמר ליה - רבינא לרב אשי: הא מילתא דעבידת קמך השתא, מי הויא אפקירותא — חוצפה — או לא?:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:13:1.english: He said to him - Ravina [said] to Rav Ashi: This matter that I did before you just now — does it constitute irreverence — insolence — or not?

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:13:2.english: “There is no wisdom,” etc. - The consideration of wisdom, honor, understanding, and [being] a counselor does not stand against the desecration of the Divine Name.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:14:1.hebrew: בפניו אסור - להורות, וחייב מיתה בידי שמים. והא דרבא לאו לאפרושי מאיסור קאי, אלא על הבא לישאל:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:14:1.english: In his presence, it is prohibited - to issue a ruling, and he is liable to death at the hands of Heaven. And this [statement] of Rava does not refer to separating [someone] from a prohibition, but rather to one who comes to ask [a question].

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:19:1.hebrew: בפניו הוה - והאי דקתני "רחוק ממנו", שהיה רחוק מקומו ממקום רבו שלש פרסאות. ומיהו, כי אורי — קמיה אורי:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:19:1.english: It was in his presence - And this that the baraita teaches, “far from him,” means that his place was three parasangs distant from his teacher’s place. However, when he ruled, he ruled in his presence.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:19:2.hebrew: והא רחוק ממנו קאמר - ואי הוראה לאו רחוק ממנו הוה, מאי אתא רבי יוחנן לאשמועינן:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:19:2.english: But didn’t he say [that he was] far from him? - And if the ruling was not [issued while he was] far from him, what did Rabbi Yoḥanan come to teach us?

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:1:1.english: Ḥarta - The name of the town.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:1:2.hebrew: דארגז - שם האיש שבנאה, והוה אמגושי. כך ראיתי בתשובת הגאונים:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:1:2.english: De’argez - [This was] the name of the man who built it, and he was a magus. So I saw in a responsum of the Geonim.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:21:1.english: I have hidden Your word - I held back my words from issuing [halakhic] rulings in a place where I would sin on their account.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:22:2.hebrew: עירא היאירי - רבו הוה, כדכתיב: ״היה כהן לדוד״ — רב לדוד:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:22:2.english: Ira the Jairite - He was his teacher, as it is written: “[he] was a priest to David” — [meaning] a teacher to David.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:24:1.hebrew: מורידין אותו מגדולתו - לעיל קאי אדזעירי, במורה הלכה בפני רבו:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:24:1.english: He is lowered from his greatness - [This] refers back to above, to [the statement of] Ze'eiri, regarding one who issues a halakhic ruling in the presence of his teacher.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:24:2.hebrew: את אחי אבא צוה - דחלק כבוד למשה, דכתיב: ״אשר צוה ה' את משה״, והורה הלכות גיעול: ״אך את הזהב״:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:24:2.english: He commanded my father's brother - For he showed honor to Moses, as it is written: “Which the Lord commanded Moses,” and [yet he] instructed [them in] the laws of purging [vessels]: “Only the gold...”

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:24:3.english: He was punished - To be lowered from [the position of] greatness that had been designated for him prior to this.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:25:1.english: As it is written: “And he shall stand before Elazar the priest, who shall inquire for him” - That Joshua was destined to need to inquire about a matter of Halakhah from Elazar.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:25:2.english: And we do not find - After the death of Moses, that Joshua had need of Elazar to ask anything.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:26:1.english: Raises an objection - [He] objects with a statement, [namely, by] issuing a halakhic ruling:

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:26:3.hebrew: כלאם - ראויים הם לכך, דהוי ליה כמורה הלכה:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:26:3.english: Shut them in - [Meaning,] they are deserving of this, which made him like one who decides halakhah [in the presence of his teacher].

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:2:1.hebrew: סר סכינא - בדק סכין לטבח. ולא אמרו להראות סכין לחכם אלא מפני כבודו של חכם, ונמצא רבינא נוטל לו עטרת כבוד העיר, ורב אשי רבו במתא מחסיא הוה, והיא מבבל:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:2:1.english: Examined a knife - He examined a knife for a slaughterer. And [the Sages] only said to show a knife to a Sage out of honor for the Sage, and thus Ravina was taking for himself the crown of honor of the city, while Rav Ashi, his teacher, was in Mata Meḥasya, which is [part] of Babylonia.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:3:1.hebrew: דהא רב המנונא אורי בחרתא דארגז - הואיל ולא היה רבו דר בה, אע"פ שהיתה בבבל; ואני לא הוריתי במתא מחסיא, שהיא מקומך:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:3:1.english: For didn’t Rav Hamnuna rule in Ḥarta De’argez - Since his teacher did not live there, even though it was in Babylonia; and I did not rule in Mata Meḥasya, which is your place.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:4:1.hebrew: תלמיד חבר - חכם כמותו, אלא שלמד ממנו דבר אחד או יותר:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:4:1.english: A disciple-colleague - [A scholar who is as] wise as him, except that he learned one thing or more from him.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:5:1.hebrew: לנפשיה - בודק סכין לשחוט בו הוא עצמו בהמה שלו, ואין צריך להראות לרבו:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:5:1.english: For himself - He examines a knife to slaughter his own animal with it himself, and does not need to show [it] to his teacher.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:6:1.hebrew: אנא מיזבן זבינא - כי אכילנא מהאי בישרא, בדמי אנא זבין לה מינך. הלכך, לאו לנפשאי, אלא כשאר טבחא הוית לי:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:6:1.english: I am buying [it] - When I eat of this meat, I am buying it from you for money. Therefore, [it is] not for myself; rather, you are to me like any other butcher.

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:8:1.hebrew: עגלא תילתא - גדל שליש, ואז הוא עומד בעיקר טעם בשרו, כדתנן (ב"מ דף סח.): "ומגדלין אותן עד שיהו משולשין", ואמרינן נמי (שם דף סט.): "מותר שליש בשכרך", אלמא: אורחיה עד שליש. ל"א: שלישי לבטן. וקשה לי הא דאמר בעלמא (סנהדרין דף סה:): "רב חנינא ורב אושעיא הוו עסקי בספר יצירה, וכל מעלי שבתא איברי להו עגלא תילתא" — דהתם, מאי "שלישי לבטן" איכא? הא לא היה בבטן מעולם:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:8:1.english: A third calf - [A calf that has] grown a third [of its full size], and then it is at the peak flavor of its meat, as we learned in a Mishnah (Bava Metzia 68a): "And they raise them until they are one-third grown"; and we also say (ibid. 69a): "The excess beyond a third is your wage," which shows that its standard [rearing] is up to a third [of its growth]. Another explanation: [It is the] third [offspring] of the womb. But this poses a difficulty for me from that which is said elsewhere (Sanhedrin 65b): "Rav Ḥanina and Rav Oshaya would occupy themselves with Sefer Yetzirah, and every Shabbat eve a third calf was created for them" — for there, what "third of the womb" is there? Behold, it was never in a womb at all!

Rashi on Eruvin 63a:9:1.hebrew: לא ליחוש לסבא - לרב אחא בר יעקב, ובתמיהה קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 63a:9:1.english: Should we not be concerned for the Elder - [This refers] to Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov; and he said [this] as a question:

Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:15:1.hebrew: מאי דרוש ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש על המזבח אע"פ שהאש יורדת מן השמים מצוה להביא מן ההדיוט - לכאורה משמע שהקטרת שהקטירו על מזבח החיצון היה, והוראת שעה היתה — כדאשכחנא בקטרת של נשיאים, כדאמרינן בשילהי התכלת (מנחות דף נ:). דאי על מזבח הפנימי הקטירו — מאי שייכא אותה דרשה לשם? והא לא היה יורד אש על מזבח הפנימי לשם קטרת, דהא קי"ל בפרק אמר להן הממונה (יומא דף לג.) דמערכה שניה שעל מזבח החיצון — לקטרת. מיהו בתורת כהנים משמע שלבית קדשי הקדשים נכנסו להקטיר, ולשם נשרפו; וצ"ע:
Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:15:1.english: What did they expound? "And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar" — although fire descends from Heaven, it is a mitzvah to bring [fire] from an ordinary [person] - Seemingly, [this] implies that the incense that they offered was on the outer altar, and it was a temporary ruling — as we find regarding the incense of the princes, as we say at the end of [the chapter] HaTekhelet (Menachot 50b). For if they offered [it] on the inner altar, how is that exposition relevant there? Behold, fire did not descend onto the inner altar for the incense, for we hold in the chapter [entitled] Amar Lahem HaMemuneh (Yoma 33a) that the second arrangement on the outer altar was for the incense. However, in Torat Kohanim it implies that they entered the Holy of Holies to offer incense, and there they were burned. And [this] requires further study.

Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:23:1.hebrew: כל הנותן מתנותיו לכהן אחד כו' - הא דקרי ליה עירא היאירי, אף על פי שהיה כהן — שמא אביו מאהרן ואמו ממנשה, כדאמר במגילה (דף יב:): "אביו מבנימין ואמו מיהודה". ופשטיה דקרא: "כהן לדוד" — לאו כהן ממש הוא, אלא שר, כמו דאמר: "ובני דוד כהנים היו" (שמואל ב ח׳:י״ח):
Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:23:1.english: "Whoever gives his [priestly] gifts to one priest, etc." - That which [the verse] calls him "Ira the Jairite," even though he was a priest — perhaps his father was [descended] from Aaron and his mother was from Manasseh, as [the Gemara] says in Megillah (12b): "His father was from Benjamin and his mother was from Judah." And the literal meaning of the verse [is that] "a priest to David" was not an actual priest, but rather a chief minister, as it states: "And David’s sons were chief ministers" (II Samuel 8:18).

Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:23:2.hebrew: מביא רעב לעולם - ואף על גב דכתיב: "על שאול ועל בית הדמים" — הא והא גרם, וסמוכין קדרש:
Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:23:2.english: Brings famine into the world - And even though it is written: "[It is] for Saul and for his bloody house" (II Samuel 21:1), both this and that caused [it], and he is expounding [the verses based on their] juxtaposition.

Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:3:1.hebrew: רב המנונא אורי בחרתא דארגז - תרי רב המנונא הוו: חד שהיה תלמידו של רב חסדא, כדמשמע הכא, ובפרק קמא דקדושין (דף כה.) גבי סבי דנזוניא, דאמר ליה רב חסדא לרב המנונא: "זיל צנעינהו"; ועוד היה אחר שהיה תלמידו של רב, כדלעיל בפרק כיצד מעברין (עירובין דף נד.), דאמר ליה רב לרב המנונא: "ברי, מדאית לך אוטיב לך":
Tosafot on Eruvin 63a:3:1.english: "Rav Hamnuna issued rulings in Ḥarta De’argez" - There were two [sages named] Rav Hamnuna: one who was a disciple of Rav Ḥisda, as is implied here and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (25a) regarding the elders of Nezonya, where Rav Ḥisda said to Rav Hamnuna: "Go and admonish them discreetly"; and there was also another one, who was a disciple of Rav, as [stated] above in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad Me’abrin (Eruvin 54a), where Rav said to Rav Hamnuna: "My son, from what you have, treat yourself well."
